title: 1Password breach: account data and source code stolen
summary: 1Password disclosed on 25 November 2026 that an attacker used an employee's corporate GitHub account, found on 19 November, to copy private source code, reach its CI/CD system and push malicious code to backend services that downloaded account records for a subset of customers. The records include names, sign-in email addresses, account identifiers and timestamps, public keys, SRP parameters and tokens from invitation, SCIM provisioning and recovery emails. 1Password says vault contents, account passwords, Secret Keys and recovery keys were not accessed, that it rotated exposed internal credentials, and that invitation and recovery codes are now ten alphanumeric characters instead of six digits.
why: The vaults are safe by design, but attackers now hold a list of confirmed 1Password users and their sign-in addresses, plus a timely pretext. Expect convincing 'security notice', invitation or recovery phishing aimed at your admins and users.
todo: Warn users that 1Password will not ask for their password, Secret Key or recovery codes, and that unexpected invitation or recovery emails should be reported.
If you use SCIM Bridge or hosted provisioning, check whether 1Password contacted you about pending invitations and review recent provisioning and recovery activity.
Keep SSO and phishing-resistant MFA on the identity provider that unlocks 1Password, since the stolen data maps people to accounts.
effective_note: Disclosed 25 Nov 2026; investigation began 19 Nov. Number of affected customers not disclosed.
